_note: Preset targets. Coordinates are ICRS degrees. pm = [pmra*cos(dec), pmdec] in mas/yr with the epoch (Julian year) of the listed position. Sources are given per entry.

targets.name: Barnard's Star
targets.blurb: The fastest-moving star in the sky: about 10.4 arcsec per year, mostly north.

track.source: Gaia DR3 (IRSA mirror); proper motion and parallax from Gaia DR3

targets.name: WISE 0855-0714
targets.blurb: The coldest known brown dwarf. NASA's coordinates are where it was around 2010; it has since moved about 2 arcminutes west.

track.source: Position: NASA challenge text (WISE epoch, about 2010.4, approximate). Motion: Luhman & Esplin 2016 (arXiv:1605.06655)

targets.name: Epsilon Indi B
targets.blurb: A pair of brown dwarfs orbiting a nearby star, drifting about 4.7 arcsec per year.

track.source: CDS Sesame/SIMBAD position (J2000); proper motion and parallax of Epsilon Indi from its Wikipedia infobox, checked against the SPHEREx images, where the predicted position lands on the source

targets.name: RW Aurigae
targets.blurb: A young variable star whose brightness changes; it does not visibly move.

targets.name: R Draconis
targets.blurb: A pulsating red giant near the north ecliptic pole, where SPHEREx looks most often.

moving.name: Makemake
moving.blurb: A dwarf planet beyond Neptune. SPHEREx saw it from opposite sides of the Sun, so its position hops by about two degrees.
moving.source: Pointing from JPL Horizons (observer: SPHEREx spacecraft, 500@-163182); used only to choose where to look
